hook.text: In 2010, analysts coined the term cord-cutting. Millions of Americans started canceling cable subscriptions.

buildup.text: Young viewers led the exodus. They'd grown up with YouTube and saw no reason to pay $100 a month for cable.

discovery.text: Netflix, Hulu, and Amazon offered most of what cable had—for a fraction of the price and with no ads.

twist.text: Cable companies fought back with data caps, price hikes, and long contracts. It only accelerated the departure.

climax.text: By 2023, more Americans streamed than subscribed to cable. The cord was officially cut.

punchline.text: Cable dug its own grave by charging too much.

quiz.question: What does 'cord-cutting' refer to?
options: Canceling cable TV subscriptions in favor of streaming
